memo.verdict: Park to watchlist, medium conviction. Not a kill: the underlying tailwind (European and Chinese salmon demand growth, tightening global supply) is real and shared by the whole CHM27 cohort, so the door stays open. Re-open at Early-Stage Assessment only once the cost programme shows sustained delivery and currency volatility eases. Explicit reassessment criteria: (1) two consecutive quarters of NOK 1bn cost-programme delivery at or above stated run-rate (NOK 173m realised Q1 2026); (2) EUR/NOK stabilising or weakening from the 10.8 level that drove the 25% EPS cut; (3) no fresh biological shock on the scale of the Q3 2025 Sjøtroll trout-maturation miss; (4) visible narrowing of the NOK 8-9/kg SalMar cost gap in the Q2/Q3 2026 print. Any two of the four criteria would justify re-triage even without full gap closure. Watchlist re-triage trigger: the Q3 2026 print (expected November 2026) or an earlier unscheduled cost-programme proof point. Explicit conviction statement: medium conviction on the park decision itself, reflecting genuine two-sided evidence rather than a clear-cut case.
case: The change thesis is real but not yet proven: a self-help cost programme plus shielding technology targets EBIT/kg growth from NOK 6.7 to NOK 11.5, a potential doubling if delivered. External change forces are genuinely strong (European fresh salmon demand +12% YoY, Chinese +28%, global supply growth slowing to 2.4% for 2026, supporting a structurally tight market) even though they are shared across the whole CHM27 cohort rather than being Lerøy-specific. Internal change forces are company-specific and credible in design: the NOK 1bn cost programme, the Cargill feed partnership, portfolio simplification (legal-entity reduction, the "Lerøy Way" standardised operating system now across nearly 100% of entities), and a new sustainability-linked incentive plan.

Valuation is statistically cheap: 8.9x forward P/E sits at the 16th percentile of Lerøy's own 10-year trading range, and this discount is only partly structural (reflecting the persistent NOK 8-9/kg cost disadvantage to SalMar), not purely cyclical. Consensus buy-side coverage is unanimous: 4 of 4 named analysts (DNB Carnegie x3, Norne x1) at BUY with tightly clustered NOK 55.00-60.00 targets.

The capital base is well-invested: CAPEX phasing down to NOK 1.7bn in 2026E from NOK 1.8bn in 2025 after intensive prior-year investment; ~30% of standing biomass was in shielded facilities at year-end 2024, rising toward half of 2026 harvest volumes; Aquatraz closed-containment systems expected to deliver first fish in Q1 2027. Volume guidance has been an "honest tracker": FY2025 Norway harvest landed at 195.6kt GWT versus 195.0kt guided (0.31% positive variance), Q1 2026 volumes within 0.25% of guidance.
counter_case: The case is undermined by a chronic, three-year pattern of missed targets that directly contradicts the "robust base" claim underpinning the change thesis. In the same twelve-month window the group missed its FY2025 harvest target (195.6kt vs 200,000 GWT guided, following a prior 2023 miss of 160kt vs 175kt guided), missed its 18.00% ROCE target (delivering only 8.00% pre-tax ROCE), and missed its Wild Catch EBIT target (NOK 270m delivered against a NOK 500m target, "due to unprecedented quota cuts"). The group also failed to achieve its stated ambition of becoming the number-one farming company on EBIT/kg. Q3 2025 operational EBIT registered at only NOK 15 million against Norne's consensus expectation of NOK 100 million, an 85% miss versus consensus, and farming operational EBIT in that quarter turned negative at NOK -306 million despite stable volume guidance. This Core Question (E1 RA2 CQ3, delivery congruency) is graded F, the weakest Core Question in the whole Element, and the memo states this history "directly contradicts" the robust-base claim.

Earnings are extremely currency-fragile: a single 4% EUR/NOK move (11.25 to 10.8) drove DNB Carnegie to cut FY2026E adjusted EPS by 25%, the single largest revision inside the entire CHM27 cohort that day, worse than Mowi (-15%), SalMar (-17%) and Bakkafrost (-9%). This is explicitly framed as "extreme earnings fragility" to a variable management does not control.
triggers: - Cost-programme proof: two consecutive quarters of NOK 1bn cost-programme delivery at or above the stated run-rate (NOK 173m realised Q1 2026 against the full-year target), evidenced in reported segment EBIT/kg.
- Currency relief: EUR/NOK stabilising or weakening materially from the 10.8 level that drove the 25% EPS cut.
- No fresh biological shock: no repeat of a Q3 2025-scale unguided biological miss (operational EBIT collapsing to 15% of consensus) in the next two reporting periods.
- Visible gap closure to SalMar: evidence in the Q2 or Q3 2026 print that the NOK 8-9/kg structural cost disadvantage is genuinely narrowing, not merely guided to narrow.
- D to C threshold: any two of the four reassessment criteria above being met would justify re-triage at Early-Stage Assessment even without full gap closure to SalMar.

- C to B threshold: a demonstrated, reported narrowing of the SalMar cost gap below NOK 5/kg, combined with a stabilising sell-side revision trend (reversing the current -2 momentum score would be the clearer signal of a genuine turn).
